previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a complex history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, tracheostomy dependence, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for sore throat, cough, chest pain, and three days of vomiting. She had recently taken levofloxacin for a prior tracheitis episode, which was discontinued due to nausea and vomiting likely caused by the antibiotic. Evaluation revealed no active infection—blood cultures were negative, and imaging showed no pneumonia. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, including IV fluids and non-opioid pain management. Hypotension and dizziness were attributed to hypovolemia, leading to temporary discontinuation of lisinopril. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to hold lisinopril until PCP follow-up, continue home medications, and attend vestibular physical therapy for dizziness.

discussed with IP, who was amenable with the plan to continue 
Augmentin and will arrange for a follow-up appointment with IP.

with saline nebs, duo nebs, and guaifenesin. She was given a few 
doses of oxycodone, but was weaned off opioid prior to 
discharge. Home tylenol, ibuprofen and gabapentin were
